author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  as a follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists each specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown by first name then last name. All specialties appear on one page. A veterinarian holding no specialty is not listed. The page is reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: the specialty directory is served at GET /specialties.html
every specialty the clinic knows is listed by its stored name
each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, by first name then last name
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarian under it
all specialties appear on one page, and no paging control is offered
specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order
the page offers no way to add, change, or remove a specialty or a veterinarian
no page of the system carries a link to the specialty directory
a clinic that knows no specialty yields a page that renders with nothing listed rather than failing
the page's user-facing wording is presented in the reader's language, per REQ-LANG-002
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory
searching, filtering, or sorting controls on the specialty directory
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1. Owner decisions quoted: 'A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2 is unchanged).' and 'The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.' No Non-Goals row was changed, so no scope_overrides entry is due: NG-2 scopes management, this requirement is a read view, and the two are coherent as written. The address GET /specialties.html is the owner's stated boundary contract; the PRD keeps it out of prose because this document names no routes anywhere and defers them to system-design.md#contracts. Three choices the request left open were taken at the narrowest reading and recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than consulted, per the owner's instruction that no further product answer will come: presentation order (narrow reading: stable, mirroring Veterinarian directory edge case 1), whether an unheld specialty is marked as such in words (narrow reading: listed with nothing under it), and whether a visible entry point follows (narrow reading: none in this slice). REQ-LANG-002 already binds every page, so the new page's wording needs a translated key in every supported language; the existing 'specialties' key may already serve.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is a fourth instance of the project's one shape: a controller reading declarative Spring Data repositories and selecting a Thymeleaf view (system-design.md#overview, ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). It lands wholly inside the existing vet package and adds no module, no layer, and no dependency. It is 'new' rather than 'minor' for one reason: the inverse Specialty-to-Veterinarian view has no mapping today, and how it is obtained is now a committed rule. Vet owns the association; Specialty holds no reference back; the inverse view is assembled in the web layer. That decision is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-unidirectional-vet-specialty-association.md and back-linked from system-design.md#contracts. Two Contracts rows are added (SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyController) and the requirement id joins the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows. Coverage claim basis: grep over the vet package and the message bundles; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so that is the weaker basis.
integration_points: New SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> in the vet package, returning every specialty in name order. Mirror PetTypeRepository: an explicit @Query with ORDER BY rather than a derived method name. Do not add @Cacheable — the vet cache has no eviction and a second cache repeats an open question (system-design.md#open-questions-from-the-survey, item 5).

New SpecialtyController in the vet package, package-private, constructor-injecting SpecialtyRepository and the existing VetRepository. One handler, GET /specialties.html, no request parameter of any kind. Divergence from the prd-entry's advisory file_targets, which named VetController: the project splits controllers by the resource served (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController all sit in one package), and a second surface on VetController would mix an unpaged read with its pagination helper. Naming follows architecture-principles.md#naming — domain noun plus Controller.

Assembly: read the ordered specialties, read VetRepository.findAll() (cached, specialties eagerly fetched), and group veterinarians under the specialties they hold. Keep this in a private method of SpecialtyController, mirroring VetController.addPaginationModel. It is model-attribute assembly, not a business rule — the architecture-principles.md Web controller bar still holds, and any actual rule that appears later moves out of the controller.

Model attribute: a LinkedHashMap<Specialty, List<Vet>> (or equivalent order-preserving structure) so the template iterates entries without re-sorting. A specialty no veterinarian holds carries an empty list rather than being absent — that is acceptance criterion 5.

New template src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html, modeled on vets/vetList.html minus the entire pagination block. Pass a layout menu name that matches no nav item (for example 'specialties') so no navigation entry is marked active; do not add a nav item to fragments/layout.html — acceptance criterion 9 forbids any link.

Wording needs no new message key. The base bundle already carries specialties, vets, name and none, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest guarantees every base key exists in all ten translated bundles. Reuse them and REQ-LANG-002 is satisfied with zero translation work. Adding a key means adding it to all eleven files or the build fails.

docs/system-design.md#contracts gains SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyController rows; the requirement id joins the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows. The route literal is deliberately NOT written into the design doc — see notes.

patterns.description: the lookup-list repository pattern to copy for SpecialtyRepository: explicit @Query with ORDER BY name, returning a List
controller shape to copy: package-private @Controller, constructor injection, private model-assembly method, view name returned as a String
table markup and the message keys to reuse (specialties, name, none); drop the pagination block below the table
test shape to copy: @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) with @MockitoBean repositories and real Vet and Specialty instances built in setup

risks.risk: Reaching for @ManyToMany(mappedBy) on Specialty to get the inverse view directly. It would surface inside the serialized veterinarian collection the second vet route returns, creating a reference cycle, and the eager fetch on the owning side would pull the reverse edge on every veterinarian read.
risks.mitigation: Ruled out in docs/adr/2026-08-21-unidirectional-vet-specialty-association.md. Specialty stays unchanged; the implementer touches neither Vet nor Specialty.

risks.risk: The page reads the whole veterinarian collection unpaged, which acceptance criterion 6 requires. An unbounded read is a reliability hazard if the roster ever stops being a small reference list.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for now and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. The clinic has no write path for veterinarians (NG-2), so the collection cannot grow from inside the application.

risks.risk: An empty specialty table must render an empty page rather than fail (edge case 3).
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf iteration over an empty collection renders nothing. Cover it with a test that stubs both repositories empty and asserts a 200 with the view name.

risks.risk: Veterinarians appearing in JPA's arbitrary set order, breaching the stable-order criterion.
risks.mitigation: Sort explicitly in the controller's assembly: veterinarians by last name, then first name, then id as tie-break. Do not add a sorted method to VetRepository — that interacts with the vets cache for no gain.

risks.risk: A hard-coded English string in the new template failing I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings.
risks.mitigation: Every text node uses th:text with a message key. Reuse the existing keys; the test walks src/main and fails the build on any literal.

notes:
DESIGN DECISIONS TAKEN AT THE NARROWEST READING, per the dispatch instruction, on the three questions the PRD left open. (1) ORDERING is a design choice, and I decide it: alphabetical by name, ascending, for specialties, matching the two existing precedents — PetTypeRepository orders its lookup list by name, and Vet.getSpecialties() sorts by name. Veterinarians under each specialty sort by last name, then first name, then id; display remains first name then last name per the requirement. Stored order is rejected: identity order is not a domain order and is not stable across the three vendor seed scripts. (2) A SPECIALTY NO VETERINARIAN HOLDS renders with the existing 'none' key in its veterinarian cell, exactly as vetList.html renders a veterinarian with no specialties. This is the consistency principle (architecture-principles.md #2), reuses a key already translated in every bundle, and satisfies 'listed, with no veterinarian under it' — no veterinarian name appears. (3) THE ABSENT ENTRY POINT is a product decision already taken in the PRD; nothing in the design contradicts it, and the implementer must not touch fragments/layout.html.

ROUTE PLACEMENT, answering the dispatch's explicit question: GET /specialties.html does NOT go into docs/system-design.md. That document names each contract once and points at the source file, and its own authoring rule forbids transcribing constant literals — every existing Contracts row describes routes in prose ('a second route', 'a fixed route') and none carries a URL. The @GetMapping annotation is authoritative for the route; the prd-entry's first acceptance criterion and the MockMvc test are what bind it. Adding the literal would be the first transcribed route in the file and would rot against the source.

SECURITY: the slice introduces no new trust boundary. The handler takes no request parameter, no path variable and no form binding, so there is no input to validate; the read is a parameterless repository call, so no injection surface exists. Rendered specialty and veterinarian names are stored data already published on the existing veterinarian page, and Thymeleaf escapes expression output by default (system-design.md#threat-model). The absent access control is NG-1 and the demonstration framing, not a new gap. Do not add a page request parameter 'just in case' — it would be an unvalidated input serving no requirement.

CHECKLIST (architecture-principles.md): placement inside the existing vet package; no reach into another package's internals; no cycle, since vet still depends only on model; both new types match In-force catalog patterns (Repository, Web controller); naming follows the domain-noun rules with no prohibited suffix; no business rule added to a controller; Specialty and Vet stay covered by the framework-mapped persistence-entity exception and are not modified; direct JPA mapping remains the sanctioned owned-both-ends case; no new dependency. Terms match ubiquitous-language.md: Specialty, Veterinarian (Vet in code and page text).

AUTOFIX AUDIT: no design-doc-autofix records exist in the handoff log, so the audit is a no-op for this dispatch.

DURABLE-MEMORY WRITES: docs/adr/2026-08-21-unidirectional-vet-specialty-association.md (new), the docs/adr/README.md index row, and docs/system-design.md#contracts — two new rows, the requirement id added to three existing rows, and one state sentence in the invariants paragraph carrying the ADR back-link.

author: review-plan-engine
rationale: risk triggers present (oversize, design-revision); full battery

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured and the reviewer has no network access. The diff adds no dependency and does not touch build.gradle, so the resolved artifact set is unchanged by this slice - a human or CI still owns the standing NVD check for Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its transitive Jackson.

Availability note, not a defect today: the directory reads the whole veterinarian roster unpaged (VetRepository.findAll) and groups it in memory at O(specialties x vets). The ADR records this as holding only while the roster stays a small reference list; if the roster ever grows or becomes externally writable, the page becomes an unbounded-allocation surface and should move behind a paged or repository-side query.
approved_aspects: No untrusted input reaches the new code: GET /specialties.html takes no path variable, request parameter, header, or body, so the injection, validation, and path-traversal classes have no entry point on this surface

All user-derived output in templates/vets/specialtyList.html goes through th:text (specialty name, vet first/last name), which HTML-escapes; no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no external resource loading, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) anywhere in the template tree

SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties uses a static @Query with no parameters and no string concatenation - no JPQL/SQL injection surface; @Transactional(readOnly = true) matches the neighbouring VetRepository pattern

SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton: the only field state is two injected repositories plus a static Comparator; the cached Vet collection from VetRepository.findAll is read through stream().sorted().toList() and Vet.getSpecialties returns a fresh sorted copy, so no shared mutable state is written per request

No new dependency, no deserialization, no file or process I/O, no logging of any value, no credentials or secrets introduced anywhere in the diff (swept for password/secret/token/key/credential across the full change set)

Route exposes only vet names and specialty names, the same data already public on /vets.html - the new endpoint widens no data boundary; absent access control is NG-1, a recorded non-goal, not a finding

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyController and SpecialtyRepository closely mirror the project's existing patterns (VetController's package-private @Controller with constructor injection and a private model-assembly helper; VetRepository's Repository<T,Integer>+@Transactional(readOnly=true) shape rather than PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository base, which fits the vet package's own precedent)
Naming follows architecture-principles.md#naming: domain noun + Controller/Repository, no prohibited suffixes

The holds() helper compares Specialty by id rather than reference, with a javadoc explaining why (specialties are read via two separate repository calls); Specialty inherits no equals/hashCode override from NamedEntity/BaseEntity, so this is a correct and defensive choice, not a stylistic one
groupHoldersBySpecialty keeps the controller handler short and readable via stream pipelines over manual loops, matching the Design Principles checklist
specialtyList.html mirrors vetList.html's markup and message-key reuse (specialties, name, vets, none) exactly, satisfying REQ-LANG-002 with no new translation burden
checkFormat and compileJava both pass clean on the change set

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD 'Done when' bullet 6 ('no page of the system carries a link to the specialty directory') is covered only by the implementer's manual diff inspection, not by a test. The implementer's stated reason -- 'a repo-wide link scan would be a brittle new test outside the slice' -- does not hold: the suite already has exactly this shape of test. I18nPropertiesSyncTest#checkNonInternationalizedStrings (src/test/java/.../system/I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java) walks every .html file under src/main with Files.walk and asserts a property text-pattern against all of them; it is not brittle and is an established, working pattern in this codebase. A same-shaped test -- walk src/main/resources/templates, assert no file contains a link/href to '/specialties.html' or 'specialties.html' as an href/th:href target -- is cheap, non-brittle by the same precedent, and turns a currently-silent regression (someone later adds a nav link) into a red test instead of a manual-inspection-only guarantee. This acceptance bullet is explicitly enumerated in prd.md and in the prd-entry's acceptance_criteria; leaving it test-free means a future violation ships silently.
findings.fix: Add a repo-scanning test (new test class or a method alongside SpecialtyControllerTests / I18nPropertiesSyncTest) that walks src/main/resources/templates and fails if any template contains an href or th:href targeting '/specialties.html'.

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 ('a clinic that knows no specialty yields a page that renders with nothing listed rather than failing') is only partially exercised. The test asserts status 200 and the view name, but never asserts that nothing is listed -- it does not check the response body at all. A regression that rendered a stray row, a null-pointer-swallowed placeholder, or leftover fixture data would still pass this test.
findings.fix: Add a body assertion, e.g. content().string(not(containsString("<td"))) or an equivalent check that the specialties table body is empty, so the test actually verifies 'nothing listed' rather than only 'did not throw'.

approved_aspects: Mocking stays within the brief: @MockitoBean on SpecialtyRepository/VetRepository under @WebMvcTest is the sanctioned web-boundary mock, and no verify(...) restates an outcome already covered by content assertions.

Test data follows the three-tier convention: RADIOLOGY_ID/SURGERY_ID/DENTISTRY_ID are named by role, vet factory methods (jamesCarter, helenLeary, lindaDouglas, carlaJenkins, alanJenkins) are meaningful named fixtures with javadoc explaining why each name was chosen (e.g. carlaJenkins/alanJenkins sharing a last name to test the last-name-then-first-name sort), no bare mystery literals.
BDD naming school followed throughout (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}); AssertJ/Hamcrest content matchers used fluently, no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue.

All three prd.md edge cases have a targeted test (specialty held by no vet; stable order by last-name-then-first-name-then-id, including a two-way tiebreak case; empty-clinic renders rather than fails), and the no-write-surface assertion (no <form>, no <input>) is correctly page-local since the shared layout fragment itself carries neither.
Dynamic check: ./gradlew test --tests SpecialtyControllerTests passes all 8 tests green.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Finding 1 (round 1) resolved with a deliberate, well-founded departure from my proposed fix: the implementer's SpecialtyDirectoryLinkAbsenceTests (src/test/java/.../vet/SpecialtyDirectoryLinkAbsenceTests.java) matches any mention of 'specialties.html' across templates rather than scoping to href/th:href. I verified this is the right call, not a weakening: fragments/layout.html's nav entries pass their route to the menuItem fragment as a plain argument (e.g. th:replace="~{::menuItem ('/vets.html','vets',...)}"), and the fragment itself carries the only th:href in the file, parameterized as @{__${link}__} -- the literal route string never appears inside an href attribute anywhere a nav link would be added. An href-scoped pattern (my original proposal) would have missed the realistic regression entirely. I reproduced red myself: inserted a menuItem('/specialties.html',...) line into layout.html, ran ./gradlew test --tests SpecialtyDirectoryLinkAbsenceTests, saw it fail with a clear message naming the offending line, then reverted (git diff --stat confirms layout.html clean) and reran green. Package placement (vet, not system beside I18nPropertiesSyncTest) is a defensible feature-ownership call; the brief states no test-package-placement rule to violate.

Finding 2 (round 1) resolved as proposed: SpecialtyControllerTests.java:191-201 theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderWhenTheClinicKnowsNoSpecialty now asserts containsString("id=\"specialties\"") and not(containsString("<td")). I reproduced the implementer's claim myself: temporarily deleted the two empty-stub given(...) lines (so the mocks fall back to the @BeforeEach non-empty fixture), reran the single test, and it failed at line 197 as expected -- the assertion genuinely bites. Reverted cleanly (git diff --stat confirms no stray changes).

Full vet-package test run (./gradlew test --tests org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet.*) is green after both reverts; working tree matches the build-pass diff exactly (git status/diff --stat show only the expected new/modified files).

No new mocking, naming, or structure issues introduced by the fix-delta: SpecialtyDirectoryLinkAbsenceTests uses no mocks (real file I/O per the brief's mocking policy), follows the BDD naming school (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldBeLinkedFromNoPage), and SpecialtyControllerTests' existing three-tier data naming and @MockitoBean usage are unchanged by the fix.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module, fourteen hunks, no sensitive paths, and no existing production file touched: three new Java/HTML sources plus two new test classes, with the only edits landing in docs. The one outward-facing addition is a new unauthenticated GET /specialties.html, and it exposes the same vet and specialty names already published on /vets.html, so it widens no data boundary.

semantic_surprise.note: The controller does exactly what its size and description imply: read specialties in name order, sort vets by last-then-first-then-id, group holders per specialty into a LinkedHashMap, render. I checked the traps and none bite - the cached Vet collection is only streamed, never mutated; holds() compares specialty ids across two repository reads rather than object identity, which is correct since Specialty inherits no equals; the layout menu name specialties matches no nav item so no navigation entry appears; every text node goes through th:text with a pre-existing message key, so no new translation debt and no unescaped output.

test_adequacy.note: Nine tests that assert real outcomes rather than restate the implementation: stringContainsInOrder pins the two-way sort tiebreak, a negative assertion pins the no-specialty vet absence, the empty-clinic case asserts an empty table body rather than only a 200, and a template-walking test guards the deliberate absence of any link, a property no request against the page could observe. The test-reviewer independently reproduced red for both of its round-1 findings before approving, which is stronger evidence than a green suite the author wrote.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers ended at approved with empty findings; the round-2 roster of code-quality, test and doc reviewers is the plan's own, so security's silence in that round is expected rather than a gap. The security approval carries two recommendations, and neither is a parked reservation about this code: the NVD note is a standing project gap on a diff that adds no dependency, and the unpaged-roster read was accepted in the ADR's Consequences before implementation and is served by the existing cached vets read.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the requirement's stated surface with nothing extra: no navigation link, no request parameter, no write path, no touch to Vet, Specialty or fragments/layout.html. Zero consultations and zero build retries; the single design revision was a bookkeeping supersede adding two missing doc paths, not a scope fight. The departure from the PRD's advisory file_targets, a new SpecialtyController instead of a second surface on VetController, was decided and reasoned in the design block and approved by the code-quality reviewer.

rationale: Purely additive slice in one package: no existing production file is modified, the new route exposes data already public elsewhere, and the tests assert ordering, absence and the empty case rather than restating the code. Confirm and merge. The one thing worth a glance is the ADR's accepted consequence that the page reads the whole vet roster unpaged.
